title: First-in first-out line read by one full cycle
summary: Written pairs join the back of a line. A fetch takes every pair from the front once and puts it on the back again, noting the first pair with the wanted address; removal does the same but does not put the matched pair back. A three-mode controller decides what is written and read.
core_idea: Keep pairs in a first-in first-out line and answer each fetch with one full cycle, under a searched three-mode controller.

state.name: Ln
state.meaning: The line: pairs (address, item) from front to back; at most C pairs.

state.name: ctl
state.meaning: Control words: the learned mode and stop symbol, the separator list Z and answer list A, the pending token p, the writing flag w and three counters c, o and d.

state.name: M
state.meaning: Learned translation from a read result to an emitted symbol, at most N entries for an alphabet of N symbols.

update.latex:
x_t=\sigma \Rightarrow w\leftarrow 0,\, o\leftarrow 0;\quad \mu=0:\; x_t\in Z \Rightarrow p\leftarrow\varnothing;\; w=1,\, p=\varnothing \Rightarrow p\leftarrow x_t;\; w=1,\, p
eq\varnothing \Rightarrow \mathrm{ins}(p, x_t),\, p\leftarrow\varnothing;\quad \mu=1:\; w=1,\, x_t
otin Z \Rightarrow \mathrm{ins}(c, x_t),\, c\leftarrow c+1;\; w=0 \Rightarrow o\leftarrow o+1;\quad \mu=2:\; x_t\in A \Rightarrow \mathrm{del}(d, \mathrm{get}(d)),\, d\leftarrow d-1;\; x_t
otin A \Rightarrow d\leftarrow d+1,\, \mathrm{ins}(d, x_t)
update.plain: per token the mode mu decides: pairs (hold one token in p, then ins the held and the new one), positions (ins under the counter c until sigma, then count emitted symbols in o), or depth (openers enter at d + 1, closers withdraw what sits at d)
update.name: controller

update.plain: ins puts the pair on the back of the line; a write that would exceed C entries is dropped
update.name: enqueue

update.latex: \mathrm{del}(a,b):\; \text{cycle every pair once, not re-entering the first with address } a
update.plain: del cycles the whole line once and leaves out the first pair whose address is a
update.name: cycle out

readout.latex: \mu=0:\; y_0=x_t,\; r_j=\mathrm{get}(y_{j-1}),\; u=r_j \text{ at the first } j\le H \text{ with } r_j\in A,\; u=r_{j-1} \text{ at the first } r_j=\varnothing;\quad \mu=1:\; u=\mathrm{get}(o);\quad \mu=2:\; u=\mathrm{get}(d);\qquad \hat{y}_t = M[u] \text{ for } u\in\mathrm{dom}\,M,\; A_0 \text{ for } u=\varnothing,\; u \text{ otherwise}
readout.plain: the current token's partner is fetched, then that partner's partner, up to H rounds, until a symbol of A appears (positions o and depths d are fetched directly in the other modes); M translates the result
readout.name: readout

readout.latex: \mathrm{get}(a):\; \text{cycle every pair from front to back once};\; \text{return the item of the first cycled pair with address } a
readout.plain: get cycles the line once (order unchanged afterwards) and returns the item of the earliest pair with address a

learning.description: Learning enumerates the controller settings, mode times stop symbol, 3(|Z| + 1) + 1 of them, where Z holds the symbols seen once in every training sequence. Each setting is run on the m items and its translation M is fitted by majority count; the best setting on the items is kept. A is read off the targets.
learning.few_shot_argument: Twelve training sequences suffice in the small cases: the wrong settings each miss several targets, the right one misses none, and M only needs each read result once.

complexity.constants_notes: A cycle moves each of at most C pairs once; at most H cycles per token.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Search over a handful of controller settings with a majority translation.

prediction.statement: With m = 12 training examples the learned controller reaches accuracy at least 0.99 on copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, nesting at depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops, on three seeds.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: String mode with C = L copies L = 8, 32, 64 over D = 4 with per-string accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = K and H = 1 answers K = 8, 32, 64 with per-query accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words (N = 2K + 17 at K = 64 with V = 16).
Nesting mode with C = depth predicts the legal closer at depth 2, 4, 8, 16 with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2T and H = 2 answers f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32 with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2(hops + 1) and H = hops + 1 resolves chains of 1, 4, 8 hops with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
The search learner reaches 0.99 from m = 12 examples on seeds 0, 1, 2 for copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops.

For any fixed capacity C, recall of K = C + 1 distinct pairs over V = 16 symbols fails on some instance: the store holds at most C pairs, so one probe's item is absent and is answered from at most 16 guesses (at C = 64 this is K = 65, above every P2 size).

toy_example.description: Three pairs in the line; a fetch returns the earliest match; a removal then exposes the next.
toy_example.python:
import json
Ln = []
def cycle(a, drop):
    found = -1
    for _ in range(len(Ln) // 2):
        k = Ln.pop(0); b = Ln.pop(0)
        if k == a and found < 0:
            found = b
            if drop:
                continue
        Ln.extend([k, b])
    return found
for a, b in [(4, 60), (5, 61), (4, 62)]:
    Ln.extend([a, b])
first = cycle(4, False)
cycle(4, True)
print(json.dumps({"get4": first, "get4_after": cycle(4, False), "line": Ln}))
